title: Event
description: One entry of the host event ledger (contract.py Event, §4, §5). Entries are append-only and hash-chained: sha256 covers the entry body plus its predecessor's hash, so an insertion, deletion, reordering or edit is detectable by re-walking the chain. host_signature carries the caller/host distinction that is the sole authority for native provenance (§5.3).

index.description: 0-based, dense, monotonic. A gap is a deleted entry.

event_id.description: Minted by the HOST, never by the subject under test.

session_id.description: Harness-reported only. A caller-minted uuid appears in a SESSION_OPEN payload, never here as if it were an ack (§10.2).

payload.description: OPEN MAP by design (§4). The payload is harness data whose keys are not knowable in advance -- §10.3 requires {"parent_session_id": "<old>"} on a fork, for one. It is validated by the driver's StreamGrammar, not here.

sha256.description: sha256(prev_hash + '\n' + canonical_json(body)) where body is this object with 'sha256' and host_signature.value removed (§5.2).

value_class.description: host-observed: the host process itself witnessed the fact. caller-asserted: the thing under test reported it -- recorded, but zero provenance weight.

key_id.description: Names the run-scoped key. NEVER the key itself.
